What if you could run at the speed of sound?
That's about twelve hundred kilometres an hour. Almost thirty times faster than Usain Bolt.
The first problem is the air. At that speed, it would push against you with a force of about five tonnes.
And you'd break the sound barrier. Everyone you pass would hear a sharp crack, like a bullet flying by.
Your reaction time is about a quarter of a second. In that time, you'd already cover eighty-five metres.
So every pole, every car, every person in your way… you'd hit before you even saw it.
And the air slamming into you would heat the front of your body by almost sixty degrees.
